blocks.content: Recognize ILS guidance and marker beacons.

items.definition: Marker beacons transmit 75 MHz vertical fan-shaped signals at fixed points along an ILS approach. Outer marker: slow dashes, blue light. Middle marker: alternating dots/dashes, amber light. Inner marker: fast dots, white light.
items.analogy: Like mile markers on a highway — fixed reference points that tell you exactly where you are on the approach.

items.definition: ILS = Localizer (horizontal/lateral guidance to runway centerline) + Glideslope (vertical guidance, nominally 3° descent path). Together they guide the aircraft to the runway in low visibility. ILS is a precision approach system.
items.analogy: Like railroad tracks leading into a tunnel — two rails (lateral and vertical guidance) that narrow to the exact landing point.

blocks.question: What does the marker beacon system provide during an ILS approach?
choices: Coded audio tones and light indications at fixed distance points on the approach
Lateral course deviation guidance to the runway centerline
Wind shear warnings based on airspeed fluctuations
blocks.feedback: Marker beacons are position-fix systems only — they tell you WHERE you are on the ILS, not how to correct your course. Localizer provides lateral guidance; glideslope provides vertical guidance. Markers add situational awareness at known distance points.

blocks.question: What two guidance signals does an ILS provide during a precision approach?
choices: Bearing and distance to the runway
Vertical and lateral wind shear alerts
Groundspeed and altitude above touchdown zone
blocks.feedback: ILS provides exactly two navigation axes: localizer (horizontal, lateral — keeps you on the runway centerline extended) and glideslope (vertical — keeps you on the ~3° descent path). These together define the precise 3D flight path to the runway.
